comments.mergedPostDetails:
Every time I open VRChat and go to the Avatars tab of the menu, it defaults to the Explore page first. Adding extra inputs and load times when wanting to change avatars. 

Once you change to the 'My Avatars' tab, the game persists that option for the remainder of the session, though it doesn't save between sessions. Even having an option to choose the default page would be better than what it is now. It's minor, but it's frustrating.
comments.mergedPostTitle: [1645] Opening Avatars menu directs to Explore page first

comments.value: A lot of people are likening this design choice to a pop-up ad that impedes basic user functionality, which is very apt. Glad our feedback is finally is being considered after the weirdly callous initial response.

While not the biggest issue, it is an unnecessary pain point and very much an example of a "dark pattern ui" whether it was intention or not. It needs to be fixed either by switching the Explore and My Avatar tabs or allowing us to set a default tab.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name} Potentially mergeable post on feature-requests board: https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/avatar-tab-should-default-to-owned-avatars-not-the-avatar-store

So they're supposedly working on testing changes.... I do genuinely hope this isn't just lip service from whoever is calling the shots behind the scenes.

I'll be blunt. I know it costs money to run and develop a game. But pushing monetization through annoying ui changes and dark patterns? That's the  kind of behavior you'd see out of a lot of mobile games, and it's one of the many reasons i stopped playing them. That and the premium currency, or the urge to paywall things. I really just don't want to see this game turn into the equivalent to one of those predatory mobile games.

@{5d6745ff863fcc6ee6ee4176|full_name}they have a lot of money from investors to pay back, on a game that is difficult to really monetize in a simple/subtle way. unfortunately, they didn't paywall avatar/world uploads from the get-go, so it's kind of too late to do that now otherwise you can bet they would have. So instead, every new feature they roll out will be somehow monetized.
